Turn 1 of 4 — read-back. Do not write any program JSON in this turn.

You are going to turn a run-of-show into a Rhylthyme program: parallel **tracks** of sequential **steps**, each with a duration and a start trigger, that one person follows against a live clock.

Plan this as a Rhylthyme run-of-show and deliver a live timeline: Session Chair's Sheet — Room 2B for one room, three speakers
Resource limits: one projector, one lapel microphone pack, one AV desk, one lectern, one foyer for catering.
Everything must be finished by coffee break at 10:30.

Source text (read all of it):
<<<
Session Chair's Sheet — Room 2B, Thursday morning

One room, one projector, one lapel pack, one AV desk, one chair. Three talks, thirty minutes each, with questions after every one. The chair calls each speaker to the lectern; nothing starts until they do.

Before the room opens
Line check at the AV desk: laptop, HDMI, house sound, record feed. 30 minutes.
Test the projector once the desk is up: resolution, keystone, the cue slide. 15 minutes.
Check the lapel pack after the projector: battery, gain, a walk to the back row. 10 minutes.

Slides
Load the first deck once the lapel pack is checked; 10 minutes, and leave it on the cue slide.
Load the second deck as soon as the first talk's questions are over; 5 minutes.
Load the third deck while the coffee is going out; 5 minutes.

The session
Chair opens the room, housekeeping and fire exits; 5 minutes.
First talk when the chair calls the first speaker: 30 minutes.
Questions after the first talk: five to ten minutes, seven is the plan.
Changeover to the second speaker: unclip the pack, clip it on, 5 minutes.
Second talk when the chair calls the second speaker: 30 minutes.
Questions after the second talk: five to ten minutes, seven is the plan.
Changeover to the third speaker once the coffee is cleared from the foyer; 5 minutes.
Third talk when the chair calls the third speaker: 30 minutes.
Questions after the third talk: five to fifteen minutes, ten is the plan.
Chair closes the session; 5 minutes.

Catering
Set the coffee station in the service corridor from ninety minutes in; 30 minutes.
Coffee goes out to the foyer when the second talk's questions end; 20 minutes.
Clear the foyer; 10 minutes.

Strike
Strike the AV desk when the chair closes; 20 minutes, cables coiled, record feed off.

Notes
The projector is the contended thing, not the room: a deck cannot be loaded while a talk is on it, so every load sits in a gap. The lapel pack is the other one, and it is the reason changeovers are real steps rather than slack. Question time is the only elastic in the morning; if the first two run long the chair trims the third.
>>>

Read all of it before you answer. Then say back, in one paragraph and in your own words: what is being made, for how many (or at what scale), by when, and under what constraints — equipment that exists only once, how many people are working, anything that has to be held, rested or ready at a particular moment. If the text you were given looks truncated, or points at a section that is not here, say so instead of filling the gap.

End your reply with the same read-back as JSON in a single ```json fenced block:

```json
{
  "summary": "one paragraph: what is being made, for how many, by when, under what constraints",
  "servesOrScale": "8 people",
  "deadline": "2026-11-26T18:00:00",
  "constraints": ["one oven", "two burners", "two cooks"]
}
```

Read-back: This is a session-chair's run-of-show for a single room (2B) on Thursday morning, hosting three speakers who each give a 30-minute talk followed by 5–15 minutes of Q&A (nominally 7, 7, and 10 minutes, with the third being the elastic buffer that gets trimmed if the first two overrun). One person — the chair — is the actor who follows the sheet, calling each speaker to the lectern (nothing starts until the chair calls it) and running the AV line-check, projector test and lapel-pack check before doors open. The single-use resources that gate the schedule are: one projector (so a deck can only be loaded while no talk is running — every "load deck" step has to fit in a gap), one lapel-mic pack (which is why speaker changeovers are real 5-minute steps, not idle time), one AV desk (for the pre-show line check and the post-show strike), one lectern, and one foyer that catering shares with the changeover-to-third-speaker step (that changeover can't happen until the foyer coffee is cleared). In parallel, a catering line sets up a coffee station 90 minutes after the top of the session, sends coffee out to the foyer as soon as the second talk's Q&A ends, and clears the foyer 10 minutes later — timed so it doesn't collide with the third changeover. The whole sequence — three talks, three Q&As, two changeovers, opening/closing remarks, slide loads, catering, and the final AV strike — must be complete by the 10:30 coffee break, though no calendar date/start time is given, only that clock time.

```json
{
  "summary": "A session chair's run-of-show for one room (2B) with three speakers, each giving a 30-minute talk followed by 5-15 minutes of elastic Q&A, bookended by AV line-check/projector/lapel-pack checks and a final AV strike, with a parallel catering line (coffee station setup, service to foyer, foyer clearing) that gates the final speaker changeover; one chair (person) runs the whole show and calls each speaker to the lectern, and everything must wrap by the 10:30 coffee break.",
  "servesOrScale": "1 room, 3 speakers, 1 chair (actor)",
  "deadline": "Thursday morning, 10:30 (time-of-day only; no calendar date or explicit session start time given)",
  "constraints": [
    "one projector (cannot be loaded/tested while a talk is running)",
    "one lapel microphone pack (changeovers between speakers are real timed steps)",
    "one AV desk (line check pre-show, strike post-show)",
    "one lectern",
    "one foyer shared by catering and the changeover-to-third-speaker step",
    "single chair/actor coordinates and gates every step (nothing starts until called)",
    "Q&A durations are elastic (5-10 or 5-15 min) and are the only slack in the schedule",
    "overall session must finish by the 10:30 coffee break"
  ]
}
```

**Model restatement:** A *track* is a single line of sequential work belonging to one thread of activity — anything that must happen at the same time as something else (a different person, a different resource, a different room) goes in its own track, and inside one track no two steps may overlap in time. Every *step* carries exactly one kind of duration: `fixed` (an exact number of seconds), `variable` (a min/max/default range for things like the elastic Q&A), or `indefinite` (open-ended until someone ends it). A *startTrigger* is how a step gets anchored to the clock or to another step's start/finish — `programStart` for t=0, `programStartOffset` for a flat delay, `afterStep`/`afterStepWithBuffer` to chain off a previous step (with an optional gap), `manual` for "wait for a human to tap go" (which fits "nothing starts until the chair calls it"), and `compound`/`onAbort` for more conditional cases. `stepId` values must be unique across the entire program, not just within a track, since triggers reference them globally. Anything that is a *shared, single-instance resource* — the projector, the lapel pack, the AV desk, the lectern, the foyer — needs a `resourceConstraints` entry with `maxConcurrent` set to how many things can use it at once (here, 1 each), and every step that names that `task` is checked against it so, e.g., a deck-load step and a talk step can't both claim the projector simultaneously. Repeated, identical work (not really present here in the "n trays" sense, since each talk/changeover/deck-load is a distinct one-off event rather than an interchangeable replicate) would instead use `replicates` on a single step rather than three hand-copied steps — but this run-of-show's three talks differ enough in surrounding context (specific speakers, specific decks) that I plan to model them as three separate steps per track rather than force them into a replicate.

Expected resource constraints (one task per line) and people: the physical single-use items are the projector, lapel pack, AV desk, lectern, and foyer — each capped at `maxConcurrent: 1`. On staffing, the text gives us the chair running the session/AV/slides thread and, separately, catering staff setting up and clearing coffee in parallel — so I'm treating this as effectively 2 actors (chair-thread + catering-thread), though the text doesn't give an explicit headcount.

```json
{
  "acknowledgement": "A track is one sequential line of work where steps never overlap; anything happening concurrently with something else belongs in a separate track. Each step has exactly one duration kind (fixed/variable/indefinite). A startTrigger anchors a step to the clock or to another step's start/end (programStart, programStartOffset, afterStep, afterStepWithBuffer, manual, onAbort, compound). stepIds are unique across the whole program. Every task a step occupies needs a matching resourceConstraints entry whose maxConcurrent enforces that shared single-instance equipment (projector, lapel pack, AV desk, lectern, foyer) can't be double-booked across tracks.",
  "resourceConstraints": [
    { "task": "avDesk", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "projector", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "lapelPack", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "lectern", "maxConcurrent": 1 },
    { "task": "foyer", "maxConcurrent": 1 }
  ],
  "actors": 2
}
```

Turn 4 of 4 — relationships, then the program.

Take the step list from turn 3 exactly as it stands.

**First, tracks.** Put each step in a track: one track per parallel line of work — per dish, per station, per instrument, per performer, per sample group. Steps in one track run one after another and must not overlap; anything that runs while something else runs belongs in its own track.

**Second, triggers.** Give every step a `startTrigger` from this vocabulary and no other:

- `{"type":"programStart"}` — at t = 0.
- `{"type":"programStartOffset","offsetSeconds":n}` — n seconds after the start; this is how a short track is delayed so it finishes with the others.
- `{"type":"afterStep","stepId":"x"}` — when x ends. Add `"offsetSeconds"` for a gap, `"event":"start"` to hang off x's start instead of its end, `"instances"` when x is replicated.
- `{"type":"afterStepWithBuffer","stepId":"x","bufferSeconds":n}` — n seconds after x ends.
- `{"type":"manual"}` — the person taps to start it: a gate that no clock can predict (guests seated, dough looks right, the surgeon is ready).
- `{"type":"compound","logic":"all"|"any","triggers":[...]}` — wait for all of, or the first of, several triggers.

**Third, refine the question before you answer it.** Within the scope of scheduling these activities for one person to follow, suggest a better version of the question "which activities depend on which, and which can run at the same time?" — one that would expose dependencies this text implies but does not state: things that must cool, rest, preheat, thaw, proof, be held warm, or be ready at the same moment as something else. Write your improved question out, answer it, and revise the triggers accordingly. A step the improved question reveals is added here, marked `"inferred": true`.

**Then emit the complete program JSON** in a single ```json fenced block: `schemaVersion`, `programId`, `name`, `environmentType`, `actors`, `tracks`, and a `resourceConstraints` entry for every `task` any step uses. Carry turn 3's provenance onto each step as `"metadata": {"sourceSpan": ..., "inferred": ...}`.

Then finish the job with the tools:
1. If the public catalog already covers this (search_public_recipes or plan_event), load that instead and stop — its result already has the live URL.
2. Otherwise keep the program you just built; `rhylthyme://guide/authoring` is the cheat-sheet and `rhylthyme://examples/*` are complete programs to pattern-match.
3. Express the limits as constraints, not as copied JSON: the `resourceConstraints`, `replicates`, `instances` and `maxInFlight` you confirmed in turn 2.
4. Run validate_program and fix every error it reports.
5. Run analyze_schedule with finishAt="coffee break at 10:30" to check the makespan, critical path and resource conflicts; adjust offsets so tracks finish together. Its `bindingConstraints` say which limit is actually gating the makespan.
6. Call visualize_schedule and give the user the live URL plus the Gantt/itinerary from the result. Do not describe the schedule in prose.
